Differentials include oncocytic carcinoid, oncocytoma, histiocytic lesions (malakoplakia, xanthogranulomatous inflammation), rhabdomyoma and squamous cell carcinoma.
entities.cyto: Brushings or FNA may show large cells with granular cytoplasm and bland nuclei, often stripped, with a granular background; the overlying atypical squamous cells may be mistaken for carcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Benign or Atypical. Aspirates or brushings show cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm, ill-defined borders and small bland nuclei, often as stripped nuclei in a granular background, which may be mistaken for histiocytes; the overlying pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia can shed atypical squamous cells mimicking squamous carcinoma.
entities.ihc: IHC is diagnostic: S100 and SOX10 strong nuclear and cytoplasmic positivity, CD68 (granular cytoplasm), inhibin, calretinin and NSE positivity, with keratin, chromogranin and synaptophysin negativity, distinguishing it from oncocytic carcinoid and carcinoma. PAS with diastase highlights the cytoplasmic granules. Ki-67 is low. Inhibin and calretinin are often positive, and Ki-67 is low; atypical or malignant forms show necrosis, mitoses, spindling and high Ki-67. Keratin is negative, which helps exclude carcinoma when pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia is present, and CD68 positivity should not lead to a diagnosis of histiocytic lesion because S100 and SOX10 are strongly positive.

entities.entity: Peripheral nerve sheath tumours of lung and airway
entities.variants: Schwannoma (endobronchial or intrapulmonary; conventional, cellular); neurofibroma (solitary or NF1-associated, plexiform); ganglioneuroma (rare); perineurioma (rare); malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour (see other sarcomas row)
entities.remarks: Rare benign neural tumours of bronchial wall or lung parenchyma; schwannomas show Antoni A and B areas with Verocay bodies; neurofibromas in NF1 may be multiple.
entities.histo: Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumours rarely arise in the lung and airways, from nerves within the bronchial wall or parenchyma, more commonly in the posterior mediastinum and only secondarily involving the lung. Endobronchial schwannoma forms a polypoid mass causing obstruction, and intrapulmonary schwannomas form circumscribed nodules. Microscopically schwannomas are encapsulated tumours with cellular Antoni A areas of spindle cells with wavy nuclei forming palisades and Verocay bodies, alternating with loose, hypocellular Antoni B areas, with thick-walled hyalinised vessels; ancient change and cellular variants occur. Neurofibromas are unencapsulated, composed of wavy spindle cells, collagen bundles (shredded carrot), mast cells and axons, and may be multiple or plexiform in neurofibromatosis type 1. Ganglioneuromas contain mature ganglion cells and Schwann cell stroma. Differentials include leiomyoma, solitary fibrous tumour, IMT, spindle cell carcinoid, synovial sarcoma, malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumour and meningioma.
entities.cyto: FNA shows cohesive fragments of bland spindle cells with wavy nuclei in a fibrillary background, sometimes with nuclear palisading, which suggests a nerve sheath tumour but is not specific. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Benign or Atypical (spindle cell lesion) pending histology.
entities.ihc: IHC shows strong diffuse S100 and SOX10 positivity in schwannoma, with collagen IV and calretinin positivity and a GFAP-positive subset; neurofibromas show patchier S100 and SOX10 with CD34-positive fibroblasts and neurofilament-positive axons. SMA, desmin, STAT6, keratin and neuroendocrine markers are negative, excluding smooth muscle tumours, SFT, synovial sarcoma and spindle cell carcinoid. H3K27me3 retention helps exclude MPNST, and Ki-67 is low.

entities.entity: Benign vascular tumours and malformations of lung
entities.variants: Capillary haemangioma (pulmonary capillary haemangioma, often incidental and multiple); cavernous haemangioma; lobular capillary haemangioma (pyogenic granuloma) of airway; lymphangioma (cystic, endobronchial); haemangioendothelioma of infancy (rare); pulmonary capillary haemangiomatosis (see PVOD row)
entities.remarks: Rare benign vascular lesions; small capillary haemangiomas are increasingly found as ground-glass nodules on CT; lobular capillary haemangioma can cause haemoptysis in airways.
entities.histo: Benign vascular tumours of the lung are uncommon. Pulmonary capillary haemangioma is a small, often incidentally detected, well-demarcated ground-glass or part-solid nodule composed of a proliferation of capillary-sized vessels within thickened alveolar septa, sometimes multiple, and must be distinguished from adenocarcinoma radiologically. Cavernous haemangiomas are composed of large, dilated, thin-walled vascular spaces with thrombi. Lobular capillary haemangioma (pyogenic granuloma) of the trachea and bronchi forms a polypoid, friable, ulcerated endobronchial lesion of lobules of capillaries in an oedematous stroma with inflammation, causing haemoptysis. Lymphangiomas are cystic lesions composed of dilated lymphatic spaces with lymphoid aggregates. Pulmonary capillary haemangiomatosis is a diffuse capillary proliferation related to PVOD and pulmonary hypertension. Differentials include arteriovenous malformation, epithelioid haemangioendothelioma, angiosarcoma, Kaposi sarcoma, alveolar adenoma (epithelial lined cysts) and haemorrhagic sclerosing pneumocytoma.
entities.cyto: FNA of vascular lesions is usually bloody and non-diagnostic, with few bland endothelial cells, and carries a bleeding risk; diagnosis relies on imaging (contrast enhancement, feeding vessels) and resection. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Non-diagnostic or Benign.
entities.ihc: IHC confirms vascular lineage: CD31, CD34 and ERG positivity in endothelial cells, D2-40 and PROX1 positivity in lymphatic channels of lymphangiomas, and SMA in pericytes. Ki-67 is low and atypia absent, unlike angiosarcoma. HHV-8 (LANA-1) is negative, excluding Kaposi sarcoma, and keratin is negative, distinguishing it from alveolar adenoma and epithelioid vascular tumours (which may express keratin focally).

entities.entity: Other benign mesenchymal tumours of lung and airway
entities.variants: Glomus tumour (tracheal and pulmonary); myopericytoma; benign fibrous histiocytoma (fibrous histiocytoma); intrapulmonary solitary fibrous tumour (see Neoplastic - Others); osteochondroma and chondroblastoma-like lesions (rare); rhabdomyoma; mesenchymal cystic hamartoma; sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma mimics; benign mesothelial inclusions
entities.remarks: Rare benign mesenchymal tumours; glomus tumour most often in trachea (SMA positive, CD34 variable, keratin negative); classify per WHO Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours.
entities.histo: Several other benign mesenchymal tumours arise rarely in the lung and airways. Glomus tumour most often involves the trachea, forming a submucosal vascular nodule composed of uniform round cells with well-defined borders, round central nuclei and eosinophilic or clear cytoplasm arranged around branching vessels, and may be mistaken for carcinoid. Myopericytomas show concentric perivascular arrangement of ovoid to spindle myoid cells. Fibrous histiocytomas show storiform spindle cells with histiocytes and giant cells. Rhabdomyomas are composed of large polygonal cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and cross-striations. Mesenchymal cystic hamartoma consists of multiple small cysts lined by respiratory epithelium with a cambium-like layer of primitive mesenchymal cells, and overlaps with type I pleuropulmonary blastoma and should be evaluated for DICER1. All are classified according to the WHO Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours volume. Differentials include carcinoid tumour, PEComa, smooth muscle tumours, nerve sheath tumours, metastatic sarcomas and their malignant counterparts.
entities.cyto: Cytology has a limited role; aspirates of these rare tumours show non-specific bland round or spindle cells and require cell block IHC. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Atypical pending histology, or Benign when diagnostic features are confirmed. Bland spindle or round cells in aspirates require cell block IHC to determine lineage, and most of these tumours are diagnosed on resection or endobronchial removal.
entities.ihc: IHC is guided by morphology: glomus tumour is SMA, h-caldesmon and collagen IV positive with pericellular staining, and negative for keratin, chromogranin, synaptophysin and INSM1, separating it from carcinoid; myopericytoma is SMA positive; rhabdomyoma is desmin and myoglobin positive; fibrous histiocytoma shows factor XIIIa and CD68 in mixed cells. Ki-67 is low. DICER1 testing is relevant for cystic hamartoma-like lesions.

entities.variants: Fetal lung interstitial tumour (FLIT) of neonates and infants; IGF1R-associated alterations reported
entities.remarks: Rare well-circumscribed solid and cystic mass of fetal-type immature lung airspaces with interstitial primitive mesenchymal cells, presenting at or soon after birth; benign behaviour after excision.
entities.histo: Fetal lung interstitial tumour is a rare tumour of neonates and young infants, presenting antenatally or shortly after birth as a well-circumscribed, solid or solid and cystic mass, often in a single lobe, causing respiratory distress. Grossly it is a spongy or rubbery, tan, circumscribed mass with small cysts. Microscopically it resembles fetal lung at the canalicular stage: irregular airspace-like structures lined by cuboidal to flattened epithelium are separated by widened interstitial septa containing uniform, round to oval immature mesenchymal cells with pale, glycogen-rich cytoplasm, resembling pulmonary interstitial glycogenosis cells. Atypia, mitotic activity and a cambium layer are lacking. The tumour has a favourable outcome after complete excision. Differentials include pleuropulmonary blastoma (cambium layer, rhabdomyoblasts, DICER1), CPAM type 3, congenital peribronchial myofibroblastic tumour (spindle cell fascicles around bronchi) and pulmonary interstitial glycogenosis (diffuse rather than mass-forming).
entities.cyto: Cytology has no role in fetal lung interstitial tumour. Not applicable to the WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology. Prenatal or neonatal aspiration is not performed, and diagnosis is based on resection of the cystic and solid mass.
entities.ihc: IHC shows that interstitial cells are vimentin positive and negative for keratin, desmin and myogenin, while the airspace lining is keratin and TTF-1 positive. PAS demonstrates glycogen. Desmin and myogenin negativity and DICER1 testing help exclude pleuropulmonary blastoma, and ALK negativity excludes IMT. The interstitial cells are glycogen-rich (PAS positive) and lack the cambium layer, rhabdomyoblasts and DICER1 alterations of pleuropulmonary blastoma; alveolar-type epithelium is TTF-1 positive. Some cases have shown ALK fusions (A2M::ALK), so ALK IHC may be useful.

entities.variants: Intrapulmonary meningioma (meningothelial, transitional, fibrous, psammomatous patterns); rare atypical or malignant forms; distinction from metastatic intracranial meningioma
entities.remarks: WHO lists under tumours of ectopic tissues; solitary well-circumscribed peripheral nodule; morphology identical to intracranial meningioma; exclude metastasis from CNS primary.
entities.histo: Primary pulmonary meningioma is a rare tumour listed in the WHO classification among tumours of ectopic tissues, presenting as a solitary, well-circumscribed, peripheral nodule, usually in middle-aged women, without a known intracranial meningioma. Grossly it is firm, grey-white and sharply demarcated. Microscopically it shows the same patterns as meningioma of the central nervous system: meningothelial whorls of syncytial epithelioid cells with indistinct borders, oval nuclei with intranuclear pseudoinclusions and fine chromatin, transitional and fibrous patterns, and psammoma bodies. Most are WHO grade 1, but atypical and malignant forms have been described. Its relationship to minute pulmonary meningothelial-like nodules is uncertain, and multiple nodules may represent diffuse meningotheliomatosis. Metastasis from an intracranial meningioma must be excluded clinically and radiologically. Differentials include minute meningothelial-like nodules (under 3 mm), solitary fibrous tumour, carcinoid tumour, sclerosing pneumocytoma, metastatic carcinoma and schwannoma.
entities.cyto: FNA shows syncytial clusters and whorls of bland epithelioid cells with oval nuclei, intranuclear inclusions and psammoma bodies, which can mimic carcinoid or adenocarcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Atypical or Suspicious for malignancy pending IHC; Benign once confirmed.
entities.ihc: IHC shows EMA, progesterone receptor and SSTR2A positivity, with vimentin positivity and usually negative keratin (focal in some secretory types), and negativity for TTF-1, chromogranin, synaptophysin, STAT6 and S100 (S100 may be focal). These findings distinguish it from carcinoid, SFT and carcinoma. Ki-67 helps grading. NF2 alterations may be detected. NF2 alterations and loss of NF2 protein occur in some cases, and the WHO CNS grading criteria (mitoses, brain-equivalent invasion not applicable, atypia, necrosis) are used to grade atypical forms. Exclusion of an intracranial or spinal primary with metastasis is necessary before accepting a primary pulmonary origin.

entities.variants: Lepidic-predominant tumour 3 cm or less with invasive focus 5 mm or less (acinar, papillary, micropapillary, solid or invasive stroma component); multifocal invasive foci summed by percentage method; pT1mi
entities.remarks: Near 100 percent disease-specific survival after complete resection; excluded if lymphovascular or pleural invasion, necrosis or STAS present; invasive size (not total size) used for T stage; not diagnosable on small biopsy or cytology.
entities.histo: Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma, non-mucinous, is a small (3 cm or less), solitary adenocarcinoma with predominantly lepidic growth and an invasive component of 5 mm or less in greatest dimension. Invasion is defined as histological subtypes other than lepidic (acinar, papillary, micropapillary, solid, or colloid, fetal and similar patterns) or tumour cells infiltrating a myofibroblastic, desmoplastic stroma. When multiple invasive foci are present, the invasive size can be estimated by multiplying the total tumour size by the percentage of invasive patterns. The diagnosis is excluded if the tumour invades lymphatics, blood vessels or pleura, contains tumour necrosis or shows spread through air spaces. The lepidic component consists of type II pneumocyte or club cell-like cells lining alveolar walls, and the invasive focus usually lies centrally. MIA is staged pT1mi and has an excellent prognosis. Complete histological examination of the resected lesion is mandatory. Differentials include AIS (no invasion), lepidic adenocarcinoma (invasion over 5 mm), collapse or sclerosis of AIS mimicking invasion (preserved elastic framework, no desmoplasia), and invasive adenocarcinoma with lepidic component.
entities.cyto: Cytology cannot diagnose MIA because the extent of invasion cannot be assessed; tumour cells from such lesions are reported as adenocarcinoma with a comment that a lepidic component may be present. Bland cells may cause underdiagnosis. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma) or Suspicious for malignancy; Atypical when cytological changes are subtle.
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1, napsin A and CK7 positivity. IHC does not measure invasion, although elastic stains (EVG) help distinguish true invasion with disruption of the elastic framework from collapsed AIS, and SMA may highlight myofibroblastic stroma. Molecular testing (EGFR and others) is not usually required for completely resected MIA but may be done in multifocal disease to establish clonal relationships.

entities.variants: Mucinous MIA (tall columnar goblet-like cells, lepidic predominant, invasion 5 mm or less); mixed mucinous and non-mucinous MIA
entities.remarks: Very rare; mucinous lepidic tumour 3 cm or less with invasion 5 mm or less; KRAS mutated; excellent prognosis; must exclude metastatic mucinous adenocarcinoma.
entities.histo: Mucinous minimally invasive adenocarcinoma is a rare small (3 cm or less) adenocarcinoma composed of tall columnar cells with abundant apical mucin and small basal nuclei, growing predominantly in a lepidic pattern, with an invasive component of 5 mm or less in which the mucinous cells infiltrate a desmoplastic stroma or form acini. As in non-mucinous MIA, the diagnosis is excluded by lymphovascular or pleural invasion, necrosis and airspace spread. Alveolar spaces are often filled with mucin, and the lesion may be solid on CT. KRAS mutations are common. Thorough sampling is needed because invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma is often multifocal and spreads aerogenously. Differentials include mucinous AIS, invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, bronchiolar adenoma (basal cells), mucinous cells in CPAM, and metastatic mucinous adenocarcinoma from pancreas, stomach, colon or ovary.
entities.cyto: Cytology cannot diagnose MIA; mucinous tumour cells are bland and may be under-called as benign goblet cells. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Atypical, Suspicious for malignancy or Malignant (mucinous adenocarcinoma). Mucin with flat sheets of deceptively bland columnar cells may be reported as benign bronchial or goblet cells; a high index of suspicion is needed when the radiological lesion is a persistent subsolid nodule, and the recommended wording is mucinous adenocarcinoma, with the extent of invasion to be determined on resection.
entities.ihc: IHC mirrors invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma: CK7 positive, frequently CK20 and HNF4-alpha positive, MUC5AC positive, TTF-1 and napsin A negative or weak, and CDX2 usually negative or focal. These features overlap with metastatic gastrointestinal and pancreatic tumours, so clinical correlation is essential. Elastic stains assess invasion. KRAS mutations are frequent and NRG1 fusions occur in some, while EGFR mutations are uncommon. Because the definition depends on invasive size of 5 mm or less, IHC and molecular tests are adjuncts only, and the lesion must be completely sampled at grossing.

entities.entity: Invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma - overview, grading and molecular subsets
entities.variants: IASLC grading system (resections): G1 lepidic predominant with less than 20 percent high-grade patterns; G2 acinar or papillary predominant with less than 20 percent high-grade; G3 any tumour with 20 percent or more high-grade patterns (solid, micropapillary, complex glandular including cribriform and fused glands); comprehensive histological subtyping in 5 percent increments; spread through air spaces (STAS); visceral pleural invasion PL0 to PL3; lymphovascular invasion; molecular subsets: EGFR-mutant (exon 19 deletion, L858R, exon 20 insertion, T790M resistance), ALK-rearranged (EML4::ALK; solid signet-ring or cribriform mucinous patterns), ROS1-rearranged, KRAS-mutant (G12C targetable), BRAF V600E and non-V600, MET exon 14 skipping and MET amplification, RET-rearranged, NTRK-rearranged, ERBB2 (HER2) mutant and amplified/overexpressed, NRG1 fusion (often invasive mucinous); adenocarcinoma, NOS; transformation to small cell carcinoma after TKI therapy; pseudomesotheliomatous adenocarcinoma (diffuse pleural growth pattern mimicking mesothelioma)
entities.remarks: Commonest lung cancer; TTF-1 and napsin A positive; histological grade, STAS and invasive size (pT) are reported; predictive biomarker testing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, HER2, PD-L1) is standard for advanced disease.
entities.histo: Invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma is the commonest type of lung cancer, occurring in smokers and, increasingly, in never-smokers, women and Asian patients, typically as a peripheral mass, sometimes with a ground-glass or lepidic component. Most tumours are heterogeneous mixtures of the five main patterns, lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary and solid, and in resections each pattern is recorded in 5 percent increments and the tumour classified by its predominant pattern. The IASLC grading system combines the predominant pattern with the proportion of high-grade patterns: grade 1 is lepidic predominant with under 20 percent high-grade patterns, grade 2 is acinar or papillary predominant with under 20 percent high-grade patterns, and grade 3 is any tumour with 20 percent or more of solid, micropapillary or complex glandular patterns (cribriform, fused glands, single cells in desmoplastic stroma). Spread through air spaces, defined as tumour cells (micropapillary clusters, solid nests or single cells) within airspaces beyond the edge of the main tumour, is a prognostic factor, especially after limited resection. Invasive size, excluding the lepidic component, is used for T staging. Visceral pleural invasion is assessed with elastic stains. Molecular subsets have characteristic but non-specific associations: EGFR-mutant tumours often lepidic or papillary in never-smoking women, ALK-rearranged tumours solid or cribriform with signet-ring cells and extracellular mucin in younger patients, and KRAS-mutant tumours in smokers, often mucinous. Differentials include metastatic adenocarcinoma (breast, colon, pancreas, thyroid, kidney), mesothelioma, epithelioid haemangioendothelioma and reactive pneumocyte hyperplasia.
entities.cyto: Cytology (EBUS-TBNA, FNA, bronchial brushing, washing, BAL and pleural fluid) is a major diagnostic and molecular testing route. Adenocarcinoma cells form three-dimensional clusters, acini and papillae, with eccentric nuclei, fine to vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli and vacuolated or finely granular cytoplasm, sometimes with intranuclear inclusions; micropapillary clusters and psammoma bodies may be seen. Cell blocks are essential for TTF-1, napsin A and predictive biomarkers (ALK, ROS1, PD-L1) and DNA or RNA for next-generation sequencing; the percentage of tumour cells should be reported. Pitfalls include reactive pneumocytes, Creola bodies, mesothelial cells and metastatic adenocarcinomas. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma, or NSCC favour adenocarcinoma), Suspicious for malignancy, or Atypical.
entities.ihc: IHC confirms lineage and guides therapy. TTF-1 (clone 8G7G3/1 more specific, SPT24 more sensitive) and napsin A are positive in about 75 to 85 percent of non-mucinous adenocarcinomas, CK7 is positive and CK20 negative; p40 is negative, separating it from squamous cell carcinoma. A limited panel conserving tissue (TTF-1 and p40, plus mucin stain) is recommended in small samples. Metastasis panels include GATA3 and TRPS1 (breast), CDX2 and SATB2 (colon), PAX8 (kidney, Mullerian), thyroglobulin (thyroid) and calretinin, WT1 and D2-40 (mesothelioma). Predictive IHC includes ALK (D5F3 or 5A4), ROS1 (D4D6, screening with FISH or NGS confirmation), pan-TRK (screening), BRAF V600E (VE1), HER2 and c-MET, and PD-L1 (22C3, SP263, SP142, 28-8) tumour proportion score for immunotherapy. EGFR mutation-specific antibodies exist but molecular testing (PCR or NGS) is the standard. Elastic stains assess pleural invasion.

entities.variants: Lepidic-predominant invasive adenocarcinoma (invasion over 5 mm, or with LVI, pleural invasion, necrosis or STAS, or size over 3 cm); grade 1 if high-grade patterns under 20 percent
entities.remarks: Non-mucinous adenocarcinoma with predominant lepidic growth but invasive component exceeding MIA criteria; favourable prognosis; EGFR mutations common.
entities.histo: Lepidic adenocarcinoma is an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma in which the predominant pattern is lepidic, that is, growth of type II pneumocyte or club cell-like tumour cells along the surface of intact alveolar walls, but which also contains an invasive component that exceeds the criteria for MIA: an invasive focus larger than 5 mm, or lymphovascular invasion, pleural invasion, tumour necrosis or spread through air spaces. The lepidic areas show crowded cuboidal to columnar cells with mild to moderate atypia, often hobnail, along slightly thickened septa, and the invasive areas show acinar, papillary, micropapillary or solid patterns or infiltration of desmoplastic stroma. Radiologically these tumours are often part-solid nodules. The term is used only for non-mucinous tumours; mucinous tumours with lepidic growth are classified as invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma. Lepidic-predominant tumours have a favourable prognosis and are IASLC grade 1 when high-grade patterns are under 20 percent. EGFR mutations are frequent. Differentials include AIS and MIA (need complete examination), collapsed lepidic growth mimicking acinar invasion, invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, metastases with lepidic growth (pancreatic, colorectal) and reactive pneumocyte hyperplasia.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows flat or slightly crowded sheets and small clusters of relatively monomorphic cuboidal cells with mild atypia, nuclear grooves or intranuclear inclusions, which may be difficult to separate from reactive pneumocytes. A lepidic pattern cannot be appreciated, and the tumour is reported as adenocarcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma), Suspicious for malignancy or Atypical.
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1, napsin A and CK7 positivity with p40 negativity. Elastic stains distinguish true invasion from lepidic growth with alveolar collapse. EGFR and other driver testing is performed according to stage and clinical guidelines, and PD-L1 testing is used for advanced disease or adjuvant immunotherapy decisions. In adjuvant settings, EGFR testing (for osimertinib) and ALK testing (for alectinib) are recommended for resected stage IB to IIIA tumours, and PD-L1 informs adjuvant immunotherapy. The invasive size, measured by excluding the lepidic component, determines the pT category.

entities.variants: Acinar-predominant adenocarcinoma; cribriform pattern (high grade, counted as complex glandular); fused glands; grade 2 or grade 3 depending on high-grade component
entities.remarks: Commonest predominant pattern; round to oval glands with central lumens infiltrating fibrous stroma; cribriform component counts toward IASLC grade 3.
entities.histo: Acinar adenocarcinoma is an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma in which the predominant pattern consists of round to oval glands with central luminal spaces, lined by cuboidal or columnar tumour cells that may contain intracellular mucin, infiltrating a fibroblastic or desmoplastic stroma. It is the most frequent predominant subtype. Tumour cells show moderate nuclear atypia and variable nucleoli. The cribriform pattern, in which tumour cells form sheets punched out by multiple back-to-back lumens without intervening stroma, and fused glands are regarded as complex glandular patterns and counted as high-grade components in the IASLC grading system; tumours with 20 percent or more high-grade patterns are grade 3. Collapse of alveoli in lepidic tumours can mimic acini, but true acini lack the alveolar elastic framework and are surrounded by desmoplastic stroma. Differentials include lepidic adenocarcinoma with collapse, papillary adenocarcinoma, metastatic adenocarcinomas (colorectal with dirty necrosis and CDX2, breast, prostate), adenoid cystic carcinoma (cribriform, myoepithelial cells) and mesothelioma with tubular patterns.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows three-dimensional clusters and acinar structures of malignant cells with eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli and vacuolated cytoplasm. Cribriform structures may be recognised. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma, or NSCC favour adenocarcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC is as for non-mucinous adenocarcinoma: TTF-1, napsin A and CK7 positive, p40 negative. Cribriform tumours with signet-ring cells and extracellular mucin should raise suspicion of ALK rearrangement, so ALK IHC (D5F3) is recommended. Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma (CK20, CDX2, SATB2 positive, TTF-1 negative) and prostatic adenocarcinoma (NKX3.1, PSA) should be excluded where clinically relevant. PD-L1 and predictive molecular testing are performed as appropriate.

entities.variants: Papillary-predominant adenocarcinoma; distinction from lepidic pattern and from micropapillary; grade 2 unless 20 percent or more high-grade patterns
entities.remarks: Glandular cells growing along central fibrovascular cores; EGFR mutations frequent; distinguish true papillae from tangentially cut lepidic growth.
entities.histo: Papillary adenocarcinoma is an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma in which the predominant pattern consists of tumour cells growing along branching central fibrovascular cores, replacing the alveolar architecture. The cells are cuboidal to columnar, with moderate atypia, and may show intranuclear inclusions and psammoma bodies. True papillae must be distinguished from lepidic growth cut tangentially, in which the tumour lines intact alveolar walls rather than forming complex branching cores within airspaces. Papillary tumours do not require myofibroblastic stroma to be considered invasive. They are graded as IASLC grade 2 unless they contain 20 percent or more of high-grade patterns. EGFR mutations are common. Differentials include lepidic adenocarcinoma, micropapillary adenocarcinoma (papillary tufts without fibrovascular cores), papillary adenoma (circumscribed, bland), sclerosing pneumocytoma, and metastatic papillary carcinomas from thyroid, kidney, ovary and breast.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows papillary clusters with fibrovascular cores, three-dimensional groups of malignant cells, nuclear inclusions and psammoma bodies; these can mimic metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma or serous carcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1, napsin A and CK7 positivity with p40 negativity. Thyroglobulin and PAX8 negativity exclude metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma (which is TTF-1 positive but napsin A negative), and PAX8 and WT1 negativity exclude Mullerian serous carcinoma. Predictive markers are tested according to guidelines. Napsin A is positive in pulmonary papillary adenocarcinoma but usually negative in thyroid carcinoma, while CK7 and TTF-1 are shared; GATA3 helps exclude metastatic breast and urothelial papillary tumours. EGFR mutations are particularly frequent in papillary-predominant tumours of never-smokers.

entities.variants: Micropapillary-predominant adenocarcinoma; filigree micropapillary pattern; high-grade pattern (IASLC grade 3 contributor); frequent STAS and lymph node metastasis
entities.remarks: Papillary tufts without fibrovascular cores floating in alveolar spaces or ring-like glands; aggressive with poor prognosis even when present as a minor component.
entities.histo: Micropapillary adenocarcinoma is an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma in which the predominant pattern consists of small papillary tufts or florets of tumour cells lacking fibrovascular cores, which float within alveolar spaces, appear detached from alveolar walls or form ring-like glandular structures. A filigree variant shows delicate, lace-like, narrow stacks of cells only a few cells wide. Psammoma bodies may be present. Micropapillary growth is a high-grade pattern associated with poor prognosis, frequent lymphovascular invasion, lymph node metastasis, spread through air spaces and recurrence after limited resection, even as a minor component, and contributes to IASLC grade 3 when 20 percent or more. Differentials include papillary adenocarcinoma (fibrovascular cores), STAS versus artefactual spread (tumour floaters), lepidic growth cut tangentially, and metastatic micropapillary carcinomas from breast, bladder, ovary and colon, which can be distinguished by IHC.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows small, cohesive, three-dimensional micropapillary clusters without fibrovascular cores, sometimes with psammoma bodies, which may resemble metastatic breast or serous carcinomas or reactive mesothelial clusters in effusions. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1, napsin A and CK7 positivity. EMA highlights reversed polarity at the outer stroma-facing surface of micropapillary clusters. GATA3 and TRPS1 (breast), GATA3 and uroplakin (urothelial), PAX8 and WT1 (ovary) help exclude metastatic micropapillary carcinomas. Predictive testing (EGFR, ALK, PD-L1) is performed as appropriate. This pattern is associated with lymphovascular invasion, spread through air spaces and early recurrence, so careful assessment of STAS and lymphatic spaces (D2-40) can be helpful. EGFR mutations and occasionally BRAF mutations are common in micropapillary-predominant tumours.

entities.variants: Solid-predominant adenocarcinoma with mucin (at least 5 cells with intracytoplasmic mucin in 2 high-power fields) or TTF-1/napsin A positivity; solid adenocarcinoma with signet-ring features (ALK); high-grade pattern; distinction from large cell carcinoma and SMARCA4-deficient tumours
entities.remarks: Sheets of polygonal tumour cells without acini or papillae; requires mucin or pneumocyte marker positivity to separate from squamous and large cell carcinoma; poor prognosis; frequent smokers, KRAS, high PD-L1.
entities.histo: Solid adenocarcinoma is an invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma whose predominant pattern consists of sheets of polygonal tumour cells lacking recognisable acini, papillae, micropapillae or lepidic growth. To qualify as adenocarcinoma, it must show intracytoplasmic mucin in at least five tumour cells in each of two high-power fields, confirmed by mucin stains, or express pneumocyte markers (TTF-1 or napsin A) on IHC. Tumour cells often have abundant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, with frequent necrosis and mitoses. Solid growth is a high-grade pattern associated with poor prognosis, smoking, KRAS mutations and higher PD-L1 expression, while solid tumours with signet-ring cells suggest ALK rearrangement. Differentials include non-keratinising squamous cell carcinoma (p40 positive), large cell carcinoma (negative for markers and mucin), LCNEC (neuroendocrine morphology and markers), thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour (BRG1 loss), NUT carcinoma, metastatic carcinomas and melanoma.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows sheets and loosely cohesive clusters of large malignant cells with prominent nucleoli and variably vacuolated cytoplasm, which may be difficult to classify without IHC. On small samples, the diagnosis is NSCC favour adenocarcinoma when based on TTF-1 or mucin positivity. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC, favour adenocarcinoma, or adenocarcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC is essential: TTF-1 and/or napsin A positive and p40 negative supports adenocarcinoma; mucicarmine or PAS-diastase demonstrates intracytoplasmic mucin. If TTF-1 and p40 are both negative, consider large cell carcinoma, SMARCA4-deficient tumours (BRG1 loss), NUT carcinoma (NUT positive), melanoma (SOX10), and metastases. ALK IHC is particularly relevant in solid signet-ring tumours, and PD-L1 testing is routine in advanced disease.

entities.variants: Lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, solid and cribriform patterns with mucinous cells; pneumonic-type (consolidative, multilobar) presentation; multifocal aerogenous spread; molecular: KRAS (commonest), NRG1 fusions, BRAF, ERBB2 alterations
entities.remarks: Tall columnar goblet-like cells with abundant apical mucin and small basal nuclei; TTF-1 usually negative, CK20 and HNF4-alpha often positive; IASLC grading not applied; mimics pneumonia; exclude GI or pancreatic metastasis.
entities.histo: Invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, previously called mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, is an adenocarcinoma composed of tall columnar goblet-type cells with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin and small, basally oriented nuclei with minimal atypia. It often grows lepidically along alveolar walls, with alveolar spaces filled by mucin, but invasive acinar, papillary, micropapillary, solid or cribriform areas are also present, sometimes with less mucinous high-grade components. It may present as a solitary nodule, multiple nodules or a pneumonic-type consolidation of one or more lobes, and spreads aerogenously and through airways, frequently producing multifocal and bilateral disease that resists surgery. KRAS mutations are frequent, and NRG1 fusions occur in a subset. The IASLC grading system for non-mucinous tumours does not apply. Differentials include mucinous AIS and MIA, colloid adenocarcinoma (abundant extracellular mucin pools), enteric-type adenocarcinoma, bronchiolar adenoma (basal layer), mucinous metaplasia in fibrosis or honeycombing, and metastatic mucinous adenocarcinomas from pancreas, stomach, colon, appendix and ovary, which can be morphologically and immunohistochemically very similar.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows abundant mucin with flat honeycomb sheets, clusters and single tall columnar mucinous cells with small nuclei, often deceptively bland and difficult to separate from benign goblet cells or bronchial contamination. Nuclear crowding, overlapping, intranuclear inclusions and grooves help. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (mucinous adenocarcinoma), Suspicious for malignancy or Atypical; under-calling is common.
entities.ihc: IHC shows CK7 positivity, with CK20 positivity in a subset (often focal), HNF4-alpha positivity and MUC5AC expression; TTF-1 and napsin A are negative or only focally positive. CDX2 is usually negative or weak, and SATB2 negative, helping exclude colorectal metastasis, but pancreatic and gastric metastases share this profile, so clinical and radiological evaluation is required. KRAS testing (including G12C), NRG1 fusion testing by RNA NGS in KRAS-wild-type tumours, and PD-L1 are relevant predictive tests.

entities.entity: Mixed invasive mucinous and non-mucinous adenocarcinoma
entities.variants: Tumour with each component (mucinous and non-mucinous) forming at least 10 percent; non-mucinous component subtyped and graded separately
entities.remarks: Each component at least 10 percent of tumour; percentage of each component and the predominant pattern of the non-mucinous component should be reported.
entities.histo: Mixed invasive mucinous and non-mucinous adenocarcinoma is diagnosed when both mucinous and non-mucinous adenocarcinoma components each constitute at least 10 percent of the tumour. The mucinous component consists of tall columnar goblet-type cells with abundant intracytoplasmic mucin and basal nuclei, as in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, and the non-mucinous component consists of cuboidal or columnar pneumocyte-type or club cell-type cells growing in lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary or solid patterns. The report should state the percentage of each component and the subtypes of the non-mucinous component, which is graded using the IASLC system. The two components often differ immunohistochemically, with TTF-1 positivity mainly in the non-mucinous part. The prognosis is intermediate. Differentials include invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma with less mucinous high-grade areas, non-mucinous adenocarcinoma with focal mucin production (mucin in solid adenocarcinoma, goblet cells), collision tumours and metastatic mucinous tumours.
entities.cyto: Cytology may show both mucinous columnar cells and non-mucinous adenocarcinoma cells, but the proportions cannot be determined; the tumour is reported as adenocarcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma). When both mucinous columnar cells and non-mucinous adenocarcinoma cells are seen, the report can mention both, but the term mixed mucinous and non-mucinous is reserved for resections in which each component forms at least 10 percent of the tumour.
entities.ihc: IHC typically shows TTF-1 and napsin A positivity in the non-mucinous component and absent or weak TTF-1 with CK20 and HNF4-alpha positivity in the mucinous component, both being CK7 positive. KRAS mutations are common. Predictive testing (EGFR, ALK, KRAS, PD-L1) is performed on the tumour, ideally sampling both components. The grading system for non-mucinous adenocarcinoma is applied to the non-mucinous component, and the two components can harbour different molecular alterations in some cases, so molecular testing should ideally sample both when results will change management.

entities.variants: Colloid-predominant adenocarcinoma; mucinous cystic tumours of low malignant potential (historical, now within colloid spectrum)
entities.remarks: Abundant extracellular mucin pools distending and destroying alveolar walls, with scant tumour cells lining fibrous septa or floating; indolent; must exclude metastatic colloid carcinoma from GI tract, pancreas, appendix, ovary.
entities.histo: Colloid adenocarcinoma is a rare adenocarcinoma in which abundant pools of extracellular mucin distend and destroy alveolar spaces, forming a gelatinous mass. Tumour cells are sparse, consisting of well-differentiated columnar or goblet-type mucinous cells, often discontinuous, lining fibrous septa at the edge of the mucin pools or floating as small clusters within the mucin. Atypia is usually mild and mitoses are rare. Tumours composed predominantly of colloid pattern are classified as colloid adenocarcinoma, while focal colloid patterns are recorded as part of other adenocarcinomas. Grossly the lesion is well circumscribed, soft and mucoid. It behaves in an indolent manner but can recur. Differentials include mucinous cystadenoma (unilocular, no invasion), invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (lepidic growth with mucin in alveoli rather than dissecting pools), and especially metastatic colloid or mucinous adenocarcinoma from colon, appendix, pancreas, breast and ovary, which must be excluded clinically.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows abundant thick extracellular mucin with sparse, bland columnar cells or small clusters, and may be reported as non-diagnostic or atypical because of low cellularity. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Atypical, Suspicious for malignancy or Malignant; Non-diagnostic if only mucin is present.
entities.ihc: IHC is often CK7 and CK20 positive, CDX2 and MUC2 positive (intestinal-type mucin), with variable or weak TTF-1, so the profile overlaps with metastatic colorectal and appendiceal mucinous adenocarcinoma. SATB2 is generally negative in pulmonary colloid carcinoma, which may help. Clinical and endoscopic exclusion of an extrapulmonary primary is required. Molecular profile includes KRAS mutations.

entities.variants: Low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma (well-differentiated fetal adenocarcinoma); CTNNB1 mutations with nuclear beta-catenin; morules
entities.remarks: Glands of glycogen-rich columnar cells resembling fetal lung (pseudoglandular stage) with subnuclear and supranuclear vacuoles and squamoid morules; younger adults; good prognosis; overlaps with epithelial component of biphasic pulmonary blastoma.
entities.histo: Low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma is a rare adenocarcinoma that resembles the developing fetal lung in its pseudoglandular stage. It usually occurs in younger adults, presenting as a well-circumscribed peripheral mass. Microscopically it shows complex branching tubules and glands lined by pseudostratified columnar cells with clear, glycogen-rich cytoplasm and subnuclear and supranuclear vacuoles, resembling secretory endometrium, with uniform round nuclei and mild atypia. Characteristic morules, solid nests of squamoid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and optically clear nuclei containing biotin, are frequently present. The stroma is benign and fibrous, unlike the malignant blastemal stroma of biphasic pulmonary blastoma. CTNNB1 mutations activate the Wnt pathway, causing nuclear and cytoplasmic beta-catenin accumulation. Prognosis is good after resection. Differentials include high-grade fetal adenocarcinoma (marked atypia, no morules, TP53 rather than CTNNB1), pulmonary blastoma (malignant primitive stroma), metastatic endometrioid carcinoma of the endometrium or ovary, and enteric-type adenocarcinoma.
entities.cyto: Cytology is rarely reported; aspirates may show clusters of columnar cells with clear cytoplasm and vacuoles and morular squamoid groups, which could suggest endometrioid carcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma) or Suspicious for malignancy. Morules may appear as cohesive clusters of bland squamoid cells without keratinisation, and cytological diagnosis is rarely attempted; differential diagnosis includes metastatic endometrioid carcinoma and pulmonary blastoma.
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1 and CK7 positivity, with aberrant nuclear and cytoplasmic beta-catenin staining that is characteristic of low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma. Neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin, synaptophysin) are often positive in scattered cells and morules. Morules are CDX2 and CD10 positive. PAX8, ER and PR are negative, which helps exclude metastatic endometrioid carcinoma. p53 is wild-type.

entities.variants: High-grade fetal adenocarcinoma; associated components of conventional adenocarcinoma, enteric or hepatoid (alpha-fetoprotein producing) differentiation; TP53 mutations; no morules
entities.remarks: Fetal-type glycogen-rich glands with marked atypia and necrosis, without morules and with membranous beta-catenin; older smokers; aggressive; may produce AFP.
entities.histo: High-grade fetal adenocarcinoma is a rare variant of adenocarcinoma composed of glands and tubules of fetal-type cells with clear, glycogen-rich cytoplasm and subnuclear or supranuclear vacuoles, like the low-grade form, but with marked nuclear atypia, frequent mitoses and necrosis, and without squamoid morules. It occurs mainly in older male smokers, and it is frequently admixed with conventional adenocarcinoma, enteric-type or hepatoid components (hepatoid adenocarcinoma with alpha-fetoprotein production may be part of this spectrum). It carries TP53 mutations rather than CTNNB1 mutations and behaves aggressively, similarly to conventional high-grade adenocarcinoma. Differentials include low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma, metastatic yolk sac tumour and hepatocellular carcinoma (AFP-producing), metastatic endometrioid or clear cell carcinoma, enteric-type adenocarcinoma and pulmonary blastoma.
entities.cyto: Cytology would show high-grade adenocarcinoma cells with clear or vacuolated cytoplasm, which cannot be specifically typed. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma). The glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm can suggest clear cell or hepatoid carcinoma and metastatic germ cell tumours, so cell block IHC for SALL4, AFP, glypican-3, TTF-1 and beta-catenin is useful; distinction from low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma requires histology.
entities.ihc: IHC shows TTF-1 positivity in many cases, CK7 positivity and membranous (not nuclear) beta-catenin. Oncofetal markers such as AFP, glypican-3 and SALL4 are frequently positive, which must not be mistaken for germ cell tumour or hepatocellular carcinoma; HepPar-1 and arginase may be positive in hepatoid areas. p53 shows mutant-type staining. Clinical exclusion of metastatic germ cell or hepatic tumours is needed.

entities.variants: Primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma with enteric differentiation (enteric component over 50 percent); adenocarcinoma with focal enteric features
entities.remarks: Resembles colorectal adenocarcinoma (tall columnar cells, cribriform glands, dirty necrosis) with at least 50 percent enteric morphology; CDX2, CK20 often positive; colorectal metastasis must be excluded clinically.
entities.histo: Enteric-type adenocarcinoma is a primary lung adenocarcinoma in which more than 50 percent of the tumour shows enteric (colorectal-type) differentiation: tall columnar cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and elongated, pseudostratified nuclei forming cribriform and acinar glands with luminal or central dirty necrosis containing nuclear debris, closely resembling colorectal adenocarcinoma. It often coexists with conventional non-mucinous adenocarcinoma components, which help establish pulmonary origin. Because morphology and IHC overlap with metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the diagnosis requires clinical exclusion of a gastrointestinal primary by colonoscopy and imaging. The tumour behaves like conventional adenocarcinoma. KRAS mutations are frequent. Differentials include metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma, invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma, colloid adenocarcinoma and fetal adenocarcinoma.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows tall columnar malignant cells in palisaded groups with elongated hyperchromatic nuclei and necrotic debris, morphologically indistinguishable from metastatic colorectal carcinoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (adenocarcinoma), with a comment recommending exclusion of colorectal primary.
entities.ihc: IHC shows at least one enteric marker positive (CDX2, CK20 or MUC2) in most cases, while CK7 is usually positive and TTF-1 is positive in about half, which favours pulmonary origin. SATB2 is typically negative in pulmonary enteric adenocarcinoma, though not reliably so. A CK7-negative, CK20-positive, CDX2-positive and SATB2-positive tumour without TTF-1 strongly favours metastatic colorectal carcinoma. Mismatch repair proteins and molecular testing (KRAS, BRAF) assist in comparison with any prior colorectal tumour.

entities.subgroup: Non-small cell carcinoma - small sample terminology
entities.entity: Non-small cell carcinoma, NOS and small biopsy or cytology categories
entities.variants: NSCC favour adenocarcinoma (TTF-1 or mucin positive, no morphological glands); NSCC favour squamous cell carcinoma (p40 positive, no keratinisation); NSCC NOS (marker-null or inconclusive); NSCC with spindle and/or giant cell carcinoma (possible pleomorphic carcinoma); adenocarcinoma with lepidic pattern (AIS not excluded); possible adenosquamous carcinoma; NSCC NOS with neuroendocrine morphology and positive markers (possible LCNEC)
entities.remarks: WHO-recommended terminology for small biopsies and cytology when resection-only diagnoses (AIS, MIA, large cell carcinoma, adenosquamous, pleomorphic) cannot be made; minimal IHC panel (TTF-1 and p40) to conserve tissue for molecular testing.
entities.histo: Most lung cancers are diagnosed on small biopsies or cytology, so the WHO classification includes standard terminology for these samples. When morphology shows clear glandular or keratinising features, the diagnosis is adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma. When a poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma lacks definite morphology, a limited IHC panel (TTF-1 and p40) and a mucin stain are used: TTF-1 or mucin positivity leads to NSCC favour adenocarcinoma, and p40 positivity with TTF-1 negativity leads to NSCC favour squamous cell carcinoma. If both markers are negative or inconclusive, the diagnosis is NSCC NOS, which should be used as rarely as possible. Terms such as AIS, MIA, large cell carcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma and pleomorphic carcinoma require resection specimens and should not be used on small samples, though comments such as adenocarcinoma with lepidic pattern, possible adenosquamous carcinoma, or NSCC with spindle or giant cell features are appropriate. Neuroendocrine markers should be used only when neuroendocrine morphology is present. The report should state whether the classification is based on morphology alone or on IHC, and indicate tumour cellularity for molecular testing. Differentials include metastatic carcinoma, mesothelioma, melanoma, lymphoma, NUT carcinoma and SMARCA4-deficient tumours.
entities.cyto: Cytology is a major route to NSCC diagnosis. Smears and cell blocks are classified using the same criteria: three-dimensional clusters and vacuolated cytoplasm favour adenocarcinoma, while dense cytoplasm, keratinisation and sheets favour squamous carcinoma; ambiguous cases are resolved by IHC on cell blocks. Rapid on-site evaluation and dedicated passes for cell blocks maximise material for molecular testing. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC favour adenocarcinoma, NSCC favour squamous cell carcinoma, or NSCC NOS).
entities.ihc: A minimal panel of TTF-1 and p40 (with mucin stain) classifies most cases while conserving tissue: TTF-1 positive and p40 negative favours adenocarcinoma, p40 diffusely positive and TTF-1 negative favours squamous cell carcinoma, and focal p40 with TTF-1 positivity still favours adenocarcinoma. In marker-null cases, additional stains (keratins, SMARCA4/BRG1, NUT, SOX10, CD45, calretinin, organ-specific markers) exclude other tumours. Predictive markers (PD-L1, ALK, ROS1) and NGS are prioritised; PD-L1 tumour proportion score is reported on cytology cell blocks with at least 100 tumour cells according to validation.

entities.entity: Squamous cell carcinoma, keratinizing (and squamous cell carcinoma, NOS)
entities.variants: Keratinizing SCC; SCC NOS; central (endobronchial) and peripheral SCC; papillary (exophytic endobronchial) growth; clear cell and alveolar space-filling patterns; molecular: PIK3CA, SOX2 and FGFR1 amplification, TP53, CDKN2A, NFE2L2/KEAP1
entities.remarks: Strongly smoking related; central mass with cavitation; keratin pearls, individual cell keratinisation and intercellular bridges; p40 positive, TTF-1 negative; paraneoplastic hypercalcaemia (PTHrP).
entities.histo: Squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumour showing keratinisation and/or intercellular bridges, or a non-keratinising tumour expressing squamous markers. It is strongly associated with smoking and usually arises centrally in segmental or lobar bronchi through a sequence of squamous metaplasia, dysplasia and carcinoma in situ, though peripheral tumours are increasingly frequent. Grossly it forms a grey-white, firm, friable mass, often with central necrosis and cavitation, obstructing the bronchus with distal atelectasis or pneumonia. The keratinizing subtype shows nests and sheets of polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic dense cytoplasm, keratin pearls, individual cell keratinisation and intercellular bridges, surrounded by desmoplastic stroma. Papillary endobronchial growth and alveolar space-filling patterns occur. Paraneoplastic hypercalcaemia from parathyroid hormone-related peptide is characteristic. Molecular alterations include TP53, CDKN2A, PIK3CA, SOX2 and FGFR1 amplification, while EGFR mutations and ALK fusions are rare, though testing is recommended in never-smokers or small samples. Differentials include metastatic SCC (head and neck, cervix, oesophagus), thymic carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, mesothelioma with squamoid features and reactive squamous metaplasia over infarcts or abscesses.
entities.cyto: Cytology from sputum, washings, brushings and FNA shows malignant squamous cells: in keratinizing tumours, pleomorphic cells with dense orangeophilic (Papanicolaou) cytoplasm, tadpole, fibre and spindle shapes, hyperchromatic pyknotic nuclei and keratin debris, often with a necrotic background. Pitfalls include reactive squamous metaplasia, keratinised vegetable cells and Pap-stained contaminants from the oral cavity. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (squamous cell carcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC is required mainly for poorly differentiated or small samples: p40 (most specific), p63, CK5/6 and desmocollin-3 are positive, and TTF-1 and napsin A are negative (TTF-1 positivity argues for adenocarcinoma). Metastatic SCC of head and neck or cervix may be p16 and HPV positive, though p16 overexpression also occurs in some lung SCC; NUT and SMARCA4 exclude rare mimics, and CD5, CD117 and PAX8 favour thymic carcinoma. PD-L1 (22C3, SP263) is tested for immunotherapy, and NGS may identify actionable alterations in never-smokers.

entities.variants: Non-keratinizing SCC; SCC with focal keratinisation below threshold
entities.remarks: No keratinisation on H&E but p40 (or p63) diffusely positive and TTF-1 negative; needs IHC for diagnosis; overlaps morphologically with solid adenocarcinoma and large cell carcinoma.
entities.histo: Non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma is a squamous cell carcinoma that lacks keratinisation and intercellular bridges on routine stains but shows immunohistochemical evidence of squamous differentiation, with diffuse p40 or p63 expression and absence of TTF-1. It forms sheets and nests of polygonal cells with moderate cytoplasm, vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei and prominent nucleoli, often with central necrosis, palisading at the edges of nests and desmoplastic stroma. Without IHC these tumours would be classified as large cell carcinoma or NSCC NOS. The clinical associations, location and molecular profile resemble those of keratinizing SCC. Differentials include solid adenocarcinoma (TTF-1 positive, mucin positive), basaloid SCC (peripheral palisading, small cells, high Ki-67), LCNEC (neuroendocrine morphology and markers), lymphoepithelial carcinoma (syncytial cells with lymphoid stroma, EBV), NUT carcinoma (abrupt keratinisation, NUT positive), thymic carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma and SMARCA4-deficient tumours.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows sheets and loosely cohesive groups of malignant cells with dense, often cyanophilic, cytoplasm and coarse chromatin, without keratinisation, and the diagnosis of squamous lineage frequently requires p40 on cell block (NSCC favour squamous). WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (squamous cell carcinoma or NSCC favour squamous cell carcinoma).
entities.ihc: IHC is diagnostic: diffuse strong p40 (and p63, CK5/6) positivity with TTF-1 and napsin A negativity. Focal p40 or p63 staining with TTF-1 positivity indicates adenocarcinoma rather than SCC. In p40-positive tumours, NUT, CD5 and CD117, GATA3 and uroplakin, and p16 with HPV testing help exclude NUT carcinoma, thymic carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma and HPV-related metastasis. PD-L1 is tested for immunotherapy.

entities.variants: Pure basaloid SCC (basaloid pattern over 50 percent); SCC with basaloid features
entities.remarks: Lobules of small to intermediate cells with peripheral palisading, high mitotic rate and comedo necrosis, p40 positive; poor prognosis; mimics small cell carcinoma and LCNEC.
entities.histo: Basaloid squamous cell carcinoma is a poorly differentiated subtype of SCC in which basaloid features account for more than 50 percent of the tumour. It forms solid lobules, trabeculae and nests of relatively small, monomorphic cells with scant cytoplasm, hyperchromatic nuclei with finely granular chromatin and inconspicuous or small nucleoli, with prominent peripheral palisading, a high mitotic rate and frequent comedo-type necrosis. Hyaline or myxoid stroma may surround the lobules, and abrupt keratinisation or areas of conventional SCC may be present. It usually arises centrally in smokers and has a poor prognosis. Differentials are mainly small cell carcinoma and LCNEC (neuroendocrine markers positive, p40 negative), adenoid cystic carcinoma (myoepithelial cells, MYB), NUT carcinoma, poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, and metastatic basaloid squamous carcinoma of the head and neck, which may be HPV related.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows cohesive clusters and sheets of small to intermediate-sized cells with high N:C ratio, hyperchromasia and palisading at cluster edges, which can closely mimic small cell carcinoma; the absence of nuclear moulding and salt-and-pepper chromatin, the presence of cohesive groups and p40 positivity on cell block help. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (squamous cell carcinoma, basaloid features).
entities.ihc: IHC is key: diffuse p40, p63 and CK5/6 positivity with TTF-1 negativity, and negative neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1), which excludes small cell carcinoma and LCNEC (although focal neuroendocrine staining can occur in a minority). NUT IHC excludes NUT carcinoma, MYB and SOX10 help exclude adenoid cystic carcinoma, and p16 with HPV testing helps identify metastasis from oropharynx. Ki-67 is high.

entities.variants: EBV-associated (most cases, Asian patients) and EBV-negative lymphoepithelial carcinoma; formerly lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma
entities.remarks: WHO 5th places under SCC; syncytial sheets of large undifferentiated cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli in dense lymphoplasmacytic stroma; EBER positive in most; young non-smoking Asians; better prognosis; high PD-L1.
entities.histo: Lymphoepithelial carcinoma is a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a variable admixture of lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, identical to undifferentiated nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and is now classified among squamous cell carcinomas in the WHO 5th edition. It occurs mainly in young to middle-aged, non-smoking patients of East Asian origin and is usually EBV associated, though EBV-negative cases occur. The tumour forms a solitary mass, often peripheral or central, without the typical smoking-related features. Microscopically there are syncytial sheets, nests and cords of large polygonal undifferentiated cells with indistinct cell borders, vesicular nuclei and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, intimately intermixed with abundant lymphocytes, plasma cells and sometimes granulomas or amyloid. Keratinisation is usually absent. It has a better prognosis than other NSCLC and frequently shows high PD-L1 expression; EGFR and other drivers are rare. Differentials include metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma (clinical examination required), lymphoma (keratin-negative), thymic carcinoma, NUT carcinoma, large cell carcinoma with lymphoid stroma and inflammatory reactions.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows syncytial clusters of large malignant cells with vesicular nuclei and macronucleoli in a background of numerous lymphocytes, which can obscure the tumour cells and mimic lymphoma or reactive lymph node in EBUS samples. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC, favour squamous cell carcinoma or lymphoepithelial carcinoma with EBER).
entities.ihc: IHC shows pancytokeratin, CK5/6, p40 and p63 positivity in tumour cells, with TTF-1 negativity, and CD45, CD3 and CD20 highlight the background lymphocytes. EBER in situ hybridisation is positive in EBV-associated cases and supports the diagnosis. PD-L1 is frequently highly expressed and relevant for therapy. Nasopharyngeal examination is needed to exclude metastasis, and NUT IHC excludes NUT carcinoma.

entities.variants: Large cell carcinoma with null immunophenotype (all markers and mucin negative); large cell carcinoma with unclear immunophenotype (focal or weak markers, or no stains available); historical variants now reclassified (large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, basaloid SCC, lymphoepithelial carcinoma, clear cell and rhabdoid phenotypes)
entities.remarks: Diagnosis of exclusion on resection only: undifferentiated NSCC lacking cytological, architectural and IHC evidence of adenocarcinoma, squamous or neuroendocrine differentiation; rare in WHO 5th; consider SMARCA4-deficient tumours and NUT carcinoma.
entities.histo: Large cell carcinoma is an undifferentiated non-small cell carcinoma that lacks the cytological, architectural and immunohistochemical features of small cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, and the diagnosis can only be made on a thoroughly sampled resection specimen. Since the WHO 2015 and 2021 classifications, most tumours previously called large cell carcinoma are reclassified as solid adenocarcinoma (TTF-1 or mucin positive) or non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (p40 positive), so true large cell carcinoma has become rare. Microscopically it shows sheets and nests of large polygonal cells with vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and moderate amounts of cytoplasm, often with necrosis, without glands, keratinisation or neuroendocrine morphology. Subsets are defined by immunophenotype: null (all markers and mucin negative) and unclear (equivocal staining or no stains done). Some marker-null tumours are SMARCA4-deficient, and others harbour KRAS or other driver mutations. Differentials include solid adenocarcinoma, non-keratinizing SCC, LCNEC, thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour, NUT carcinoma, pleomorphic carcinoma, melanoma, lymphoma, germ cell tumours and metastases.
entities.cyto: Large cell carcinoma cannot be diagnosed on cytology or small biopsies; cells of such tumours, large and undifferentiated with prominent nucleoli, are reported as NSCC NOS when marker negative. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC NOS). The cytological pattern of large, undifferentiated malignant cells with abundant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei and macronucleoli overlaps with solid adenocarcinoma, non-keratinizing squamous carcinoma, LCNEC, melanoma, SMARCA4-deficient tumours and lymphoma, so cell blocks with a wide marker panel are needed. Material should also be saved for PD-L1 and molecular testing, since many such tumours are later reclassified.
entities.ihc: IHC is required to make the diagnosis: TTF-1, napsin A, p40, CK5/6 and mucin stains are negative or equivocal, and neuroendocrine markers negative. BRG1 (SMARCA4) and BRM (SMARCA2), NUT, SOX10, CD45, SALL4, OCT4 and organ-specific markers are recommended to exclude SMARCA4-deficient tumours, NUT carcinoma, melanoma, lymphoma, germ cell tumours and metastases. Keratin confirms epithelial nature. PD-L1 and molecular testing (KRAS, others) are performed for therapy.

entities.variants: Adenosquamous carcinoma (each component at least 10 percent); EGFR-mutant and KRAS-mutant subsets
entities.remarks: Both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma components, each forming at least 10 percent of tumour on resection; worse prognosis than either alone; EGFR mutations in a subset (test for drivers).
entities.histo: Adenosquamous carcinoma is a carcinoma containing both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma components, each comprising at least 10 percent of the tumour, and the diagnosis requires a resection specimen. The components may be intermixed or separate, with glandular structures (acinar, papillary, solid with mucin) adjacent to keratinizing or non-keratinizing squamous nests. The squamous component should be confirmed by keratinisation or p40, and the glandular component by architecture, mucin or TTF-1. It accounts for a few percent of lung cancers, is usually peripheral, and has a worse prognosis than pure adenocarcinoma or SCC. EGFR mutations and other drivers occur in a subset, so molecular testing is recommended. Differentials include mucoepidermoid carcinoma (central, intermediate cells, no keratinisation, MAML2 fusion), squamous cell carcinoma with entrapped benign glands or pneumocytes, adenocarcinoma with squamous metaplasia, and collision tumours. On small biopsies, the term possible adenosquamous carcinoma may be used in a comment.
entities.cyto: Cytology may show both malignant glandular and squamous cells, but the proportions cannot be assessed, so the term adenosquamous should be used cautiously, usually as NSCC with both features. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC, with comment). Cell block IHC may show separate TTF-1-positive and p40-positive cell populations, which is more reliable than morphology; if only one component is sampled, the report should not exclude adenosquamous carcinoma, and a definitive diagnosis is left to resection.
entities.ihc: IHC confirms the two components: the squamous cells are p40 and CK5/6 positive and TTF-1 negative, whereas the glandular cells are TTF-1 and napsin A positive and p40 negative. MAML2 rearrangement testing helps exclude mucoepidermoid carcinoma when the morphology is ambiguous. Molecular testing (EGFR, KRAS, ALK) and PD-L1 are performed. Co-expression of TTF-1 and p40 within the same cells favours adenocarcinoma with focal p40, not adenosquamous carcinoma. EGFR mutations, when present, are usually shared by both components, supporting a common origin, and should be tested because they are targetable.

entities.variants: Pleomorphic carcinoma (NSCC with at least 10 percent spindle and/or giant cells, or composed only of spindle and giant cells); MET exon 14 skipping mutations enriched; KRAS, high PD-L1
entities.remarks: Poorly differentiated NSCC with sarcomatoid component of at least 10 percent; aggressive; resection-only diagnosis; test for MET exon 14 skipping.
entities.histo: Pleomorphic carcinoma is a poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma, usually adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, that contains at least 10 percent spindle cells and/or giant cells, or a carcinoma composed purely of spindle and giant cells. It is a subtype of sarcomatoid carcinoma, occurs mainly in older male smokers, tends to be large and peripheral, invades the chest wall, and has a poor prognosis. Microscopically there is a conventional carcinoma component (glands, squamous nests or solid sheets) admixed with fascicles of malignant spindle cells and bizarre, large, multinucleated or mononuclear giant cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, frequent emperipolesis of neutrophils, necrosis and vascular invasion. Heterologous elements are absent (if present, the tumour is carcinosarcoma). MET exon 14 skipping mutations are enriched, along with KRAS and TP53 mutations and high PD-L1 expression. Differentials include sarcomas (primary or metastatic), mesothelioma (sarcomatoid), carcinosarcoma, pulmonary blastoma, melanoma, SMARCA4-deficient tumours and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour.
entities.cyto: Cytology may show pleomorphic malignant giant cells and atypical spindle cells, sometimes with a recognisable carcinoma component, but the diagnosis of pleomorphic carcinoma requires resection; small samples are reported as NSCC with spindle and/or giant cell features. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC with sarcomatoid features, or malignant neoplasm NOS).
entities.ihc: IHC confirms epithelial differentiation: pancytokeratin, CK7 or EMA expression in at least some spindle or giant cells, with TTF-1 in the adenocarcinoma component and p40 in the squamous component. Keratin may be focal or absent in sarcomatoid areas, so multiple keratins should be used. Calretinin, WT1 and D2-40 help exclude sarcomatoid mesothelioma, while SOX10 and S100 exclude melanoma, BRG1 excludes SMARCA4-deficient tumours, and ALK excludes IMT. MET exon 14 testing (NGS) and PD-L1 are important predictive tests.

entities.variants: Pure spindle cell carcinoma (sarcomatoid carcinoma composed only of spindle cells)
entities.remarks: Rare; carcinoma composed entirely of malignant spindle cells without other differentiation; keratin expression needed; resection-only diagnosis; mimics sarcoma and sarcomatoid mesothelioma.
entities.histo: Spindle cell carcinoma is a rare form of sarcomatoid carcinoma composed purely of malignant epithelial spindle cells, without a differentiated carcinoma component or giant cells. It forms fascicles and storiform arrays of atypical spindle cells with hyperchromatic, pleomorphic nuclei, frequent mitoses and necrosis, often with an inflammatory infiltrate. It is mostly seen in older smokers and behaves aggressively. Because there is no differentiated component, the diagnosis depends on IHC demonstration of keratin expression and exclusion of sarcoma and mesothelioma, and it can be made with certainty only on resection. Differentials include primary and metastatic sarcomas (synovial sarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, MPNST, intimal sarcoma), sarcomatoid mesothelioma invading lung, melanoma (spindle cell or desmoplastic), inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour and spindle cell carcinoid.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows malignant spindle cells singly and in fascicles, which cannot be distinguished from sarcoma without IHC. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (malignant spindle cell neoplasm, with recommendation for histology and IHC). Cell blocks should be prepared for keratin, TTF-1, p40, calretinin, STAT6 and SOX10 staining. Cytology from pleural fluid may be paucicellular because sarcomatoid cells shed poorly, and the absence of an epithelial component does not exclude carcinoma.
entities.ihc: IHC is essential: positivity for one or more keratins (AE1/AE3, CAM5.2, CK7) and EMA confirms carcinoma, while TTF-1 may be positive in some. Calretinin, WT1, D2-40 and BAP1 or MTAP loss help with mesothelioma, SOX10 and S100 with melanoma, desmin and SMA with smooth muscle tumours, TLE1 and SS18::SSX testing with synovial sarcoma, MDM2 with intimal sarcoma, and ALK with IMT. MET exon 14 skipping should be tested.

entities.variants: Pure giant cell carcinoma (sarcomatoid carcinoma composed almost entirely of tumour giant cells)
entities.remarks: Rare, highly aggressive; large pleomorphic multinucleated and mononuclear tumour giant cells with neutrophil emperipolesis; discohesive; resection-only diagnosis.
entities.histo: Giant cell carcinoma is a rare form of sarcomatoid carcinoma composed almost entirely of highly pleomorphic, mononuclear and multinucleated tumour giant cells, without a differentiated adenocarcinoma or squamous component. The cells are large, discohesive, with abundant eosinophilic, sometimes foamy cytoplasm, bizarre, lobulated nuclei, macronucleoli and frequent atypical mitoses, and they often contain engulfed neutrophils (emperipolesis). A dense inflammatory infiltrate of neutrophils and extensive necrosis are common. It behaves very aggressively with early metastasis. Differentials include pleomorphic carcinoma (more than giant cells), choriocarcinoma (hCG positive syncytiotrophoblast), anaplastic large cell lymphoma, melanoma, pleomorphic sarcomas, giant cell-rich metastatic tumours (thyroid anaplastic carcinoma, adrenal cortical carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma) and SMARCA4-deficient tumours.
entities.cyto: Cytology shows large, bizarre, discohesive malignant giant cells with macronucleoli and emperipolesis of neutrophils in a necrotic inflammatory background. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (NSCC with giant cell features). The cells may show emperipolesis of neutrophils, multiple nuclei and bizarre forms, and the differential includes choriocarcinoma, anaplastic lymphoma, melanoma, pleomorphic sarcomas and metastatic anaplastic carcinomas of thyroid or pancreas; cell blocks for IHC are required.
entities.ihc: IHC shows keratin and often vimentin positivity, with TTF-1 positivity in some cases. hCG and SALL4 exclude choriocarcinoma, CD30 and ALK with CD45 exclude anaplastic large cell lymphoma, SOX10 excludes melanoma, and BRG1, PAX8, HepPar-1 and SF-1 help exclude other mimics. MET exon 14 testing and PD-L1 are performed. A high proportion of cases have MET exon 14 skipping or KRAS mutations, and PD-L1 expression is often high, which may be relevant for therapy. Absence of a conventional component in a resection is required for the diagnosis of pure giant cell carcinoma.

entities.variants: Classic biphasic pulmonary blastoma (low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma-like epithelium with primitive blastemal stroma); heterologous elements (cartilage, osteoid, rhabdomyoblasts); CTNNB1 mutations; DICER1 mutations in some
entities.remarks: Rare biphasic tumour of adults resembling fetal lung, with malignant fetal-type glands and primitive mesenchymal stroma; nuclear beta-catenin; distinct from pleuropulmonary blastoma of children.
entities.histo: Pulmonary blastoma is a rare biphasic malignant tumour that recapitulates the embryonic lung, consisting of an epithelial component resembling low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma and a primitive, blastemal mesenchymal component. It occurs mainly in adults in the fourth and fifth decades, often smokers, as a large peripheral mass, and behaves aggressively. The epithelial component forms branching tubules of glycogen-rich columnar cells with subnuclear and supranuclear vacuoles and squamoid morules, as in low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma. The stroma consists of densely packed, small, oval to spindle primitive cells with scant cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, often condensed around the glands, and may contain heterologous elements such as immature cartilage, osteoid or rhabdomyoblasts. CTNNB1 mutations with nuclear beta-catenin in both components are characteristic, and DICER1 mutations are reported in some. Differentials include pleuropulmonary blastoma (children, cystic or solid sarcoma without malignant epithelium), carcinosarcoma (high-grade conventional carcinoma with sarcoma), low-grade fetal adenocarcinoma alone, synovial sarcoma (biphasic), metastatic Wilms tumour and teratoma.
entities.cyto: Cytology may show two populations: clusters of columnar epithelial cells and primitive small round to spindle cells, which may be misinterpreted as small cell carcinoma or sarcoma. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant (malignant neoplasm, with comment on biphasic features).
entities.ihc: IHC shows the epithelial component positive for keratins, EMA and TTF-1, with neuroendocrine markers in morules and scattered cells, and the blastemal stroma positive for vimentin with variable SMA, desmin and myogenin in rhabdomyoblastic areas. Nuclear and cytoplasmic beta-catenin in both components is characteristic. WT1 and PAX8 negativity helps exclude metastatic Wilms tumour, and TLE1 and SS18 testing exclude synovial sarcoma.

entities.variants: Carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements (rhabdomyosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma) and conventional carcinoma (squamous, adenocarcinoma, large cell)
entities.remarks: Mixture of NSCC and true sarcoma with heterologous differentiation; older male smokers; central or peripheral; poor prognosis.
entities.histo: Carcinosarcoma is a malignant tumour composed of a mixture of non-small cell carcinoma, most often squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma, and true sarcoma containing heterologous elements such as malignant cartilage, bone or skeletal muscle. It occurs mainly in older male smokers, as central endobronchial polypoid tumours or peripheral masses, and has a poor prognosis. Microscopically the carcinoma component consists of conventional squamous nests or glands, intermixed with or juxtaposed to a high-grade sarcoma of spindle cells containing rhabdomyoblasts, malignant chondroid or osteoid. Unlike pulmonary blastoma, the epithelium is not of fetal type and lacks morules. Differentials include pleomorphic carcinoma (no heterologous elements), pulmonary blastoma, biphasic synovial sarcoma, metastatic carcinosarcomas (from uterus or ovary), teratoma with malignant transformation and primary sarcomas of lung with entrapped epithelium.
entities.cyto: Cytology may show both malignant epithelial cells and malignant mesenchymal cells, sometimes with chondroid matrix or rhabdomyoblasts, but a definitive diagnosis requires resection. WHO Reporting System for Lung Cytopathology category: Malignant.
